info.name: Four Crowns
info.description: Chess for four players on a cross shaped 14x14 board of 160 squares, with four armies of sixteen pieces attacking each other at the same time. Capturing enemy pieces and checkmating opponents scores points, and the player with the most points when only one king is left standing wins. Turn order, captures and scorekeeping are done by the table.
info.helpText:
Seats Four players, one per corner panel: Red plays first, then Blue, Yellow and Green, going clockwise around the board. The big coloured tile on the left and the glowing seat both show whose turn it is.

Moving Just drag your pieces. No move is ever refused and legal moves are not checked, so promotions, castling and en passant are done by hand.

Capturing Drop a piece on top of an enemy piece: the table moves the captured piece into your capture tray and adds its value to your score (pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 5, rook 5, queen 9, king 20 - the values are listed on the right).

Score buttons Every panel has -1 / +1 for corrections and a +20 button for the checkmate or stalemate bonus. The score field itself can also be typed into.

Skull button Marks a player as out. Their army turns grey, stays on the board as an obstacle and is worth no points any more, and their seat is skipped in the turn order. Press it again to bring the player back.

Skip button Passes the turn to the next player without moving a piece.

Gear button Switches all table automation off (green = on, grey = off): no capturing, no scoring and no turn passing, so you can set up a position by hand. Press it again to switch it back on.

Queen + button Puts an extra piece of any colour next to the board - pick the piece in the overlay. Use it to promote a pawn (drag the new piece onto the pawn's square); the extra pieces disappear again when the game is restarted.

Restart button Sends every piece home, sets all scores to 0 and gives the turn back to Red.

Board The four coloured lines across the board are the promotion rows: a pawn promotes when it reaches the line in its own colour. The tinted squares are each player's home camp.
